metadata.title: Trump pushes Clarity Act at White House crypto meeting

content.text:
President Donald Trump hosted cryptocurrency executives at the White House on Wednesday and pressed Congress to pass the Digital Asset Market Clarity Act, sending Bitcoin and related stocks higher.
"We need Congress to take the next step by passing the Clarity Act, a fair version of the Clarity Act," Trump said, according to Bloomberg. "It's a very, very powerful structured legislation which will keep us ahead of China, keep us ahead of everyone else." Trump also said the U.S. was at the "very beginning of a revolution" in finance.
Among those joining Trump at the White House, according to Bloomberg, were Coinbase Global CEO Brian Armstrong, Gemini Space Station Inc.'s Tyler and Cameron Winklevoss, Payward Inc. co-CEO Arjun Sethi — whose firm runs the Kraken exchange — and Vlad Tenev of Robinhood Markets. Securities and Exchange Commission Chairman Paul Atkins and Commodity Futures Trading Commission Chairman Michael Selig also attended.
Bitcoin climbed roughly 5% to approximately $71,880 in the aftermath of the meeting, while Ether jumped more than 9%, reaching $2,288.91. Coinbase stock jumped close to 8% in premarket trade Thursday, according to The Wall Street Journal. Strategy shares gained 9.4%, extending a 13% advance from Wednesday, and Mara Holdings rose 5.5%.
Trump also said the CFTC was working to bring decentralized exchange Hyperliquid into the U.S. "in a fully compliant legal fashion," according to The Wall Street Journal. Hyperliquid's token surged roughly 25% in the preceding 24 hours, while Hyperliquid Strategies stock jumped 30% in the prior session and added another 7.5% in premarket trading Thursday.
A separate macro catalyst also boosted crypto markets: the U.S. Treasury announced it would increase buybacks of 20-year and 30-year bonds, pushing yields lower and lifting demand for higher-risk assets.
The Clarity Act has stalled in the Senate ahead of a critical September 15 procedural vote amid a dispute between Democrats and Republicans over ethics provisions, including how to enforce a ban on government officials operating crypto businesses. The bill cleared the Senate Banking Committee in May and passed the House in July 2025. Senators are anticipated to revisit the bill around September 14, though that window amounts to only 14 working days before an October election recess.
With congressional action uncertain, federal regulators have moved to fill the gap with agency-level rules. The SEC has proposed exempting certain digital asset offerings from securities registration requirements. The CFTC's newly formed Innovation Advisory Committee, whose membership spans Coinbase, Robinhood Markets, and prediction-market platforms Kalshi Inc. and Polymarket, is scheduled to convene for the first time on Thursday. Industry supporters have warned that agency rules, while welcome in the near term, remain vulnerable to reversal by a future administration.
